entries.clue: Bill Cash, left out, mixed a drink (7)

indicators.note: L, the abbreviation for left, is dropped from the letters
the remaining letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: BILL CASH with one L (left) removed

annotation.surface: Veteran Tory Eurosceptic Bill Cash, excluded from the gathering, mixes himself a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: Bill Cash is a long-serving Conservative MP, so the name looks like a person; it is just letters. Only one of the two Ls goes.
annotation.definitionFit: Chablis is a dry white wine from Burgundy.

entries.clue: Provocative revelation: band joined by Josh (10)

blocks.note: a strip is a narrow band

annotation.surface: A news report of some provocative revelation about a band and someone called Josh.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Josh' reads as a man's name; it is the verb meaning to rib or tease.
annotation.definitionFit: A striptease is a provocative act in which the performer gradually reveals the body.

entries.clue: Penny extra almost put off (8)

indicators.note: MORE is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: to daunt is to discourage or put off

annotation.surface: A penny extra nearly deters a buyer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a coin; it is Penny Mordaunt, the Conservative politician.
annotation.definitionFit: Penny Mordaunt is a Conservative MP and former cabinet minister, so her surname completes 'Penny'.

entries.clue: Help needed with testicle – foul! (8)

blocks.note: to give a hand is to help

annotation.surface: Someone crying foul after help with a testicle, a crude football-injury scene.
annotation.walkthrough: In football (soccer), handling the ball is an offence, so 'foul!' is the definition rather than an exclamation of disgust.
annotation.definitionFit: Handball is the football foul of touching the ball with the hand or arm.

entries.clue: Position with inferior goods imported by South America (6)

indicators.note: TAT is brought inside S and US

annotation.surface: A comment on a country's standing when it imports shoddy goods into South America.
annotation.walkthrough: 'South America' reads as the continent; it is two separate abbreviations sitting either side of the cheap goods.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: your status is your standing or rank in a society or organisation.

entries.clue: see 23dn. (4)
Talks lovingly about politician initially eager to score (7)

indicators.note: COOS goes about, that is all around, the politician
only the first letter of 'eager' is used

blocks.note: to coo is to murmur fondly

annotation.surface: A smooth-talking politician flirts, keen to score.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Score' reads as sexual conquest; it is the verb for writing music.
annotation.definitionFit: To score a piece of music is to compose or arrange it.

entries.clue: The latest party gaffe: leader serves up fast food (3,3)

indicators.note: the leader of 'gaffe' is its first letter

annotation.surface: News of a party's latest blunder: its leader handing out fast food.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Party' and 'leader' suggest politics; the party is a celebration (DO) and the leader is just a first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A hot dog is a sausage in a bun, classic fast food.

entries.clue: Nuts to go as such a singer (8)

definitions.text: Nuts to go as such a singer

blocks.note: reads as a dismissive exclamation or a snack being cleared away; really slang for testicles that must be removed
reads as any vocalist; really the boy singer castrated to keep his high voice

annotation.surface: A singer is told they must lose their testicles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' reads as an exclamation or as food; it is slang for testicles, which such a singer loses before his voice breaks.
annotation.definitionFit: A castrato was a male singer castrated before puberty to keep a high voice.

entries.clue: Foodstuff – you surprise me, getting rid of it (4)

indicators.note: IT is removed from NO SHIT

blocks.note: 'no shit' is a sarcastic 'you don't say'

annotation.surface: Someone marvels at a foodstuff as they throw it away.
annotation.walkthrough: The expression is the ironic 'no shit!'; lose its IT and food remains.
annotation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British slang for food.

entries.clue: Eye cover showing pissed female veteran (9)

blocks.note: blind drunk; pissed is British slang for drunk

annotation.surface: An Eye cover story shows an elderly woman roaring drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eye cover' looks like the front page of Private Eye, where this puzzle runs; it is a covering for the eyes. In British English pissed means drunk, not angry.
annotation.definitionFit: A blindfold is a strip of cloth tied over the eyes.

entries.clue: Pert bust concealing wife's dope (5)

indicators.note: PERT is broken into a new order
the rearranged letters hide W inside them

blocks.note: anagram of PERT, split as T and ERP

annotation.surface: A pert bust hides the fact that a wife is on drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bust' pretends to be a bosom and 'dope' a drug; one is the anagram signal and the other a fool.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are mild British insults: a dope is a stupid person and a twerp a silly, annoying one.

entries.clue: Nit's awful painful expression, being abreast of the news (2,5)

indicators.note: NIT is made a mess of, giving INT

annotation.surface: An idiot pulls a pained face at keeping up with current events.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Painful expression' suggests a grimace; it is the word you exclaim.
annotation.definitionFit: To be in touch is to be up to date with what is happening.

entries.clue: One asserts one's missing what's needed as an Eye crossword solver (7)

definitions.text: what's needed as an Eye crossword solver

indicators.note: the A (one) is left out of SWEARS

annotation.surface: A self-referential boast from someone who claims to lack what an Eye crossword needs.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue is about this very puzzle in Private Eye; 'one' is used twice, first as AN and then as the A that goes missing.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone solving the Eye crossword needs the answers.

entries.clue: Government head after us – misses visual aid (10)

indicators.note: the head of 'Government' is its first letter
'after' places G behind EYE, so EYE is written first

blocks.note: 'us' is the magazine speaking: Private Eye

annotation.surface: A political complaint that the head of government, following the Eye's lead, fails to see.
annotation.walkthrough: Private Eye refers to itself, so 'us' is EYE. 'Misses' looks like a verb (fails); it is the plural of 'miss', a girl.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: eyeglasses, the American word for spectacles, exist to help you see.

entries.clue: A toilet fitted with a CCTV on top of roof, whose main aim is to keep undesirable party out? (8,5)

definitions.text: whose main aim is to keep undesirable party out?

indicators.note: the letters are fitted together in a new arrangement
only the top of 'roof', its first letter, is added

blocks.note: used as it stands, as fodder
used as it stands, as fodder

annotation.surface: A security-conscious toilet with a camera on its roof, meant to keep out unwanted partygoers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks like revellers kept out of a loo; it is a political party. The surface sets up a nightclub picture.
annotation.definitionFit: A tactical voter backs whichever candidate is best placed to beat the party they most dislike.

entries.clue: Doubt about your first, almost pleasant, doctrine (8)

indicators.note: the first letter of 'your'
NICE loses its last letter

blocks.note: c. for circa, Latin for about
an ism is a doctrine or creed

annotation.surface: Musings on doubting a first, almost pleasant, belief.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like it wraps something; here it is simply C, from circa.
annotation.definitionFit: Cynicism is a general distrust or doubt of others' motives.

entries.clue: Like coming from Cairo with MG crashing outside Pyramids finally (8)

indicators.note: CAIRO and MG are smashed into a new order
the rearranged letters go around S
the final letter of 'Pyramids'

blocks.note: anagram of CAIRO MG, split as ORGA and MIC

annotation.surface: An MG sports car coming from Cairo crashes outside the pyramids.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coming' reads as travelling; the definition is sexual. MG is a British car make.
annotation.definitionFit: Orgasmic means relating to orgasm, that is, to coming.

entries.clue: Caught inside, Thomas screwed bear (7)

indicators.note: C goes inside the rearranged letters
THOMAS is twisted into a new order

blocks.note: anagram of THOMAS, split as STOMA and H

annotation.surface: A lurid report of a man named Thomas caught in a compromising position with a bear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal; it is the verb to tolerate.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: food you can stomach stays down, so by extension to stomach anything is to tolerate it.

entries.clue: Not right to arrest college and university staff? (7)

indicators.note: FAULTY seizes C and holds it inside

annotation.surface: A protest that arresting college and university staff is wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'university staff' is a loose definition: a faculty is a department and its teachers.
annotation.definitionFit: A faculty is a university division and, by extension, the body of lecturers in it, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: Rogue senator's betrayal (7)

indicators.note: SENATOR goes rogue, its letters out of line

annotation.surface: A rogue senator betrays his country.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true of the answer, which makes 'Rogue' look like a description rather than an instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: treason is the gravest form of disloyalty, against one's sovereign or state.

entries.clue: Sun, low grade paper – makes you cry (6)

blocks.note: a C is a mediocre exam grade
a ream is 500 sheets of paper

annotation.surface: The Sun is a low-grade paper that would make anyone weep.
annotation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, so 'low grade paper' reads as a jibe at it; the paper is a REAM and the grade a C.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: a scream is the shrillest way to cry out.

entries.clue: "After knocking back drink, one needs a show of kingly status" (7)

indicators.note: LAGER is turned back to front

annotation.surface: A quotation: after downing a drink, a person needs to show off like royalty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knocking back' reads as downing the drink; here it also tells you to turn the word round.
annotation.definitionFit: Regalia are the emblems of royalty, such as crown and sceptre, displayed as signs of kingly status.

entries.clue: (& 6dn.) A rare dog doctored – violent argument on the way (4)

indicators.note: the letters are tampered with and rearranged

annotation.surface: A rare dog has been neutered, and a violent argument follows on the journey.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs on into 6 down. 'Doctored' suggests a vet neutering the dog; it means tampered with.
annotation.definitionFit: Road rage is violent anger between drivers on the road.

entries.clue: Ex-PM hurt over 'little woman' (5)

indicators.note: MAR lies over JO, covering it on both sides

blocks.note: Jo March, heroine of the novel Little Women

annotation.surface: A former prime minister wounded by being called 'the little woman'.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Little woman' looks like a patronising term for a wife; the quotation marks point to Jo, one of Alcott's Little Women. John Major was British PM from 1990 to 1997.
annotation.definitionFit: John Major is a former British prime minister.

entries.clue: Shock scrap involving LibDem leader (4)

indicators.note: to involve is to enfold or include, so JOT takes L inside it
the leader of 'LibDem' is its first letter

blocks.note: a jot is a tiny amount

annotation.surface: Shock over a fight involving the Liberal Democrat leader.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' suggests a fight and 'LibDem leader' a politician; they are a tiny amount and a single letter. The Liberal Democrats are a UK party.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a jolt is a sudden jarring shake, physical or emotional.

entries.clue: EU's cause failed after country's first dictator (9)

indicators.note: EUS CAUSE falls apart into a new order
the rearranged letters come after C
the first letter of 'country'

annotation.surface: A Brexit-era lament that Europe's cause collapsed after a national strongman came first.
annotation.walkthrough: Nicolae Ceausescu was the communist dictator of Romania, overthrown and executed in 1989.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Ceausescu held absolute communist power over Romania from 1965 until 1989.

entries.clue: Officer's grabbing genital area by end of the fold (8)

indicators.note: COL'S grabs LAP and holds it inside
only the last letter of 'the' is used

blocks.note: COL, colonel, plus the S of the possessive
the lap, where the thighs meet when seated

annotation.surface: An officer groping someone's crotch in a sheep fold.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fold' looks like a pen for sheep; it is the verb meaning to give way.
annotation.definitionFit: To fold is to collapse, as a business or a person under pressure.

entries.clue: Think it's cool, playing set? Think over (6)

indicators.note: SET is played about with to give EST

blocks.note: with the opening 'Think', to dig something is slang for thinking it's cool

annotation.surface: A musician wonders whether their set is cool, then reconsiders.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Think it's cool' reads as an opinion; it is the slang verb 'dig'.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: as the stomach digests food, the mind digests an idea by mulling it.
